name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 369 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 369 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: Security forces held an anti-fidayeen drill at a railway station in Kulgam while a landmine blast on the LoC in Poonch killed four terrorists, including a LeT commander. In South Kashmir a man was injured in a bear attack and another man was injured in a separate bear incident. In Manipur the Makui Village Authority condemned firing and demanded immediate security intervention, while supporters marched to a BJP headquarters and staged a home sit-in. A missing head of a Naga man killed in a Manipur attack was recovered after five days. The conflict produced 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Sikkerhetsstyrker holdt en anti-fidayeen-øvelse på en jernbanestasjon i Kulgam mens en landmineeksplosjon på LoC i Poonch drepte fire terrorister, inkludert en LeT-kommandør. I Sør-Kashmir ble en mann såret i et bjørnangrep, og en annen mann ble såret i en separat bjørn-hendelse. I Manipur fordømte Makui Village Authority skytingen og krevde umiddelbar sikkerhetsintervensjon, mens støttespillere marsjerte til et BJP-hovedkvarter og holdt en hjemme-sitt-in. En savnet leder av en Naga-mann som ble drept i et angrep i Manipur ble funnet etter fem dager. Konflikten førte til 437 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
